segments.title: Fast-firing guns against torpedo boats
segments.body: The starting point was the familiar problem of stopping torpedo boats. The Royal Navy's answer to E-boats was to bring fast-firing guns to bear. The same response is proposed for modern small-boat attacks.

evidence.note: The summary identifies fast-firing guns as the answer to torpedo boats and small-boat attacks.

segments.summary: The Royal Navy treated E-boat defence as the familiar torpedo-boat problem and answered it with fast-firing guns.

segments.title: Reaction speed against E-boat ambushes
segments.body: Engaging a threat at long range is preferable when detection permits it. E-boats were intended to behave as ambush predators and deny defenders that warning distance. Their small size and use of crowded shipping lanes could conceal their approach. Night attacks were another problem when defenders lacked radar. Even where radar was available, attackers could try to spoof the early sets and preserve surprise. Defenders therefore needed to react quickly enough to drive off or destroy an E-boat once it appeared.

evidence.note: Small size, crowded shipping lanes, night attacks without radar, and attempts to spoof early radar limit warning time. Rapid reaction is needed to drive off or destroy the attacker.

segments.summary: Small targets, crowded shipping lanes and darkness reduced warning time, while absent radar or attempts to deceive early sets complicated E-boat detection.

segments.title: Gunboats and destroyers against E-boats
segments.body: The Royal Navy answered the E-boat threat with numerous gun-armed craft. Steam Gun Boats and Fairmile D craft were examples, and destroyers also appear among the response options. These gunboats differed from the older Insect class, whose vessels nevertheless had some success against E-boats in one or two encounters. The shared requirement was enough firepower that could be brought into action quickly against an E-boat.

evidence.note: The response includes Steam Gun Boats, Fairmile D craft and destroyers. Insect-class gunboats had some success in one or two encounters, while the main requirement is firepower that can be deployed quickly.

segments.summary: Steam Gun Boats, Fairmile D craft and destroyers offered firepower that could be brought into action quickly against E-boats.

segments.title: Why small escorts carried anti-aircraft guns against E-boats
segments.body: The heavy gun armament of some small escorts can look like a provision for air defence. Some of their rapid-firing weapons were intended to deal with E-boats that came close enough to engage. Those guns could still be described as anti-aircraft weapons. Their designation therefore does not by itself explain the surface threat that helped determine an escort's armament.

evidence.note: Small escorts carried rapid-firing weapons to deal with E-boats at close range, even where the guns were billed as anti-aircraft weapons.

segments.summary: Some rapid-firing weapons on small escorts were intended to counter nearby E-boats even when described as anti-aircraft guns.
